clue.text: Governor of fortress has woman put in prison

indicators.note: the woman's name is placed inside the word for prison, so 'put in' signals a container

parts.note: can is slang for prison
Stella is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A fort's governor sends a woman to jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A castellan is the keeper or commander of a castle, its appointed governor.

clue.text: Carbon said to be in hard material

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
oral means spoken, said rather than written

explanation.surface: Carbon is reported to be present in some tough substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' looks like a sound signal, but here it is just a synonym: ORAL, spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is the stony skeleton built up by tiny sea creatures, a hard reef-forming substance.

clue.text: One showing acceptable standard, repeatedly circling ring in stern working out

indicators.note: the whole par-ring-par group sits inside the rearranged letters of stern, so 'in' marks a container
working out suggests the letters of stern being worked into a new order
the two copies of the standard go round the word ring, so 'circling' signals a container
repeatedly tells us to take the word for acceptable standard twice

parts.note: par is an acceptable or normal standard, as in 'up to par'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone meeting the required standard again and again while training in a boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles the standard and 'circling' wraps it round the ring; 'working out' scrambles stern, and 'in' sets the group inside. 'One showing' points to the boxer's training partner, so the definition is the bare 'One'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparring partner is a person who boxes with a fighter in training, so the bare 'One' points to such a person.

clue.text: English girl, flippant, dismissing one messenger

parts.note: miss is a young unmarried woman, a girl

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the letter for one is taken out of the word for flippant

parts.note: airy means casual or flippant
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A frivolous English girl sends someone packing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing one' removes I from AIRY, leaving ARY.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is an envoy sent on a mission, carrying a message for someone.

clue.text: Cattle I'd diverted with grids

indicators.note: the herd is sent another way, hinting that these letters are turned into a different order

explanation.surface: Livestock that I had rerouted through gridded gates.
explanation.definitionFit: Something latticed has a criss-cross pattern of strips, a grid-like framework.

clue.text: That is fellow's set-up, see

indicators.note: in a down clue 'set up' means raised, so the word for fellow is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: man is a fellow; the 's joins it to what follows
Ely is a cathedral city whose bishop's diocese is a see

explanation.surface: Here is the arrangement of the man's business, take a look.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely, in Cambridgeshire, is the classic crossword see.
explanation.definitionFit: Namely introduces a specification, just as 'that is' (i.e.) does.

clue.text: Philosopher became stuck, unable to reach conclusion

indicators.note: the phrase means the word for became stuck stops short of its final letter

parts.note: locked means jammed fast, stuck

explanation.surface: A thinker got stuck and could not finish his argument.
explanation.walkthrough: LOCKED loses its last letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: John Locke was the seventeenth-century English empiricist thinker.

clue.text: It may be for external application, but fool laps it up

definitions.text: It may be for external application

indicators.note: laps here means wraps around, so the word for fool encloses the other piece

parts.note: a loon is a silly person, a fool

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word it is written from the bottom, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something meant for outside use, yet an idiot drinks it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laps it up' suggests drinking, but 'up' turns 'it' round and 'laps' means wraps around; the definition reads as a riddle about something rubbed on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion is a liquid rubbed onto the skin, applied externally rather than taken internally.

clue.text: Possibly a "pic-generator", him? That's one's deduction

definitions.text: Possibly a "pic-generator", him? That's one's deduction

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged otherwise, so they are rearranged
deduction means taking away, so the letter for one is subtracted from the letter pool

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a man who makes pictures must be a film person.
explanation.walkthrough: A + PICGENERATOR + HIM has the answer's letters plus an extra I; 'one's deduction' removes that I and 'Possibly' rearranges the rest. The whole clue also describes the film-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinematographer is the director of photography on a film, the person who produces the moving pictures.

clue.text: Vengeful females with our union chaps on fateful day

parts.note: EU is the European Union, 'our' union from a British setter's view at the time
men are chaps
the Ides of March was the day Caesar was killed, the classic fateful day

explanation.surface: Avenging women join our union's men on an ominous date.
explanation.walkthrough: IDES recalls the Ides of March, when Julius Caesar was assassinated.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eumenides are the Furies of Greek myth, female spirits who punish wrongdoers.

clue.text: In sleep Arab maybe is no dreamer

indicators.note: the Arab's name is placed in the word for sleep, so 'In' marks a container

parts.note: rest is sleep or repose
Ali is a common Arab name, so an Arab may be called Ali

explanation.surface: An Arab caught napping is no fantasist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' could be a horse; here it stands for a man called ALI, set inside REST.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist deals with things as they are, the opposite of a dreamer or idealist.

clue.text: Bumped into, on my returning glass for a drink, maybe?

parts.note: met means encountered, bumped into

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word my is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone ran into me and took my glass back for a refill.
explanation.walkthrough: Saying 'a glass' to mean the drink in it is the textbook example of this figure of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A metonym names something by an associated thing, as 'glass' stands for its contents.

clue.text: Field and house in London

definitions.meaning: ... cricket ground in London, a famous playing field
the House of ..., the upper chamber of Parliament at Westminster

explanation.surface: A pitch and a building in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is the London cricket ground; the House of Lords is the upper house of the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both the St John's Wood cricket ground and the upper parliamentary chamber.

clue.text: Peel is part of it if a lemon's taken apart

indicators.note: taking something apart breaks it up, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

parts.note: read as 'lemon is', the s counts as a letter

explanation.surface: Lemon rind becomes a component when you dismantle the fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peel' looks like rind, but it is a town on the Isle of Man, the self-governing island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Peel is a town on the west coast of this Irish Sea island, so it is a part of it.

clue.text: Various things source of heat takes moisture from

parts.note: the sun is our main source of heat
dries means removes moisture from

explanation.surface: The sun evaporates the water from all sorts of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundries are miscellaneous small items, assorted bits and pieces.

clue.text: Sign of penitence shown by group in church after act of pillage

indicators.note: after places the church group's word following the pillage word

parts.note: a sack is the plundering of a captured town
the cloth means the clergy as a body

explanation.surface: Penance shown by the clergy following a raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' is a traditional term for the clergy collectively.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing rough sacking garments was the biblical show of repentance, as in 'sackcloth and ashes'.

clue.text: Bolt from the stable

definitions.meaning: a metal fastener, a kind of bolt
an establishment where horses are kept for breeding

explanation.surface: A horse escapes from its stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' suggests a horse running off, but it is the fastener; the stable is the breeding farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is both a short threaded fastener and a horse-breeding establishment.

clue.text: Murder victim strangled by artist is French writer

indicators.note: the victim is gripped round by the artist's letters, so 'strangled by' signals a container

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
Abel was killed by his brother Cain, the first murder victim in Genesis
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter throttles someone in a French novelist's crime story.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword staple for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: François Rabelais was the sixteenth-century French author of Gargantua and Pantagruel.

clue.text: A person taking steps, very restricted progress-maker

indicators.note: restricted means held in, so the letter for very is confined inside the other words

parts.note: a dancer takes steps

explanation.surface: Someone stepping out, though heavily constrained, still moves forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A person taking steps' reads as a definition but gives A DANCER, which holds V.
explanation.definitionFit: One who advances is someone moving forward, making headway.

clue.text: Manage to find special cloak

definitions.meaning: to deal with things successfully, to get by
a long ceremonial cape worn by clergy

explanation.surface: Get by in a particular cape.
explanation.definitionFit: Cope means to handle difficulties, and also a priest's vestment worn on special occasions.

clue.text: Company takes a long time to provide first-aid items

parts.note: a band is a company or group of people
ages means a very long time

explanation.surface: A firm is slow to supply first-aid kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandages are strips of fabric for dressing wounds, a staple of a medical kit.

clue.text: Son getting fat or "thickset"?

parts.note: tubby means plump, fat

explanation.surface: A boy putting on weight, or just stocky?
explanation.definitionFit: Stubby means short and thick, much as a stocky build is.

clue.text: Disgraced when caught in a plot

indicators.note: the word for when is trapped inside the other pieces, so 'caught in' means a container

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Shamed after being found in a conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a conspiracy; it is a flower BED.
explanation.definitionFit: Abased means humiliated or lowered in esteem, brought into dishonour.

clue.text: On which hearts may be laid bare?

definitions.text: On which hearts may be laid bare?

parts.words: On which hearts may be laid bare?
parts.note: sounds like a confessional place for emotions, but the hearts are playing cards put face up on a surface

explanation.surface: Somewhere people pour out their feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearts' are a suit of cards, and laying cards down is what you do on this piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A card table is a folding table where players set down cards, hearts among them.

clue.text: A wood without water initially becomes flooded

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the A and wood surround the first letter

parts.note: ash is a kind of tree and its timber

indicators.note: initially means at the start, taking the first letter of water

explanation.surface: A forest with no water still ends up underwater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: A and ASH go round W.
explanation.definitionFit: Awash means covered with water, inundated.

clue.text: The man with destiny to be downtrodden?

definitions.note: the clue's adjective stands for a downtrodden person, a noun

parts.note: he is the male pronoun, the man
lot means one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: Is it a man's fate to be oppressed?
explanation.walkthrough: The helots were the serf class of ancient Sparta; the question mark allows the adjective for the person.
explanation.definitionFit: A helot was a Spartan serf, the archetype of an oppressed underclass.

clue.text: See return of vessel in a sec — one conveying passengers

indicators.note: return means come back, so the whole run of vessel, in and a sec is read backwards

parts.note: a sub, or submarine, is a vessel
a mo, short for moment, is a sec

explanation.surface: Watch a ship come back in a moment carrying travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' reverses the whole run SUB+IN+MO; 'See' just invites you to look.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus is the full old name for a bus, a public vehicle carrying passengers.

clue.text: Henry's coming in unflustered after a litre — lager, perhaps

indicators.note: after places the cool-with-Henry piece behind the a and litre
the Henry letter enters the word for unflustered, so 'coming in' signals a container

parts.note: cool means calm, unflustered
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry stays calm after a litre of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The henry is the SI unit of inductance, symbol H.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a beer, and beer is an example of an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Writer only just managing to put out short line

indicators.note: put out means expelled, so the letter for line is removed

parts.note: hardly means barely, only just
L is a short form of line

explanation.surface: An author scarcely coping after shortening a line.
explanation.walkthrough: HARDLY loses its L.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy was the English novelist and poet of Wessex.

clue.text: Tommy's seen to abscond more than once

parts.note: desert means run away from duty, abscond
to rat is to desert, to run off from one's side

explanation.surface: A British soldier is seen running away twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than once' tells you to use 'abscond' twice. A Tommy is a British soldier; the Desert Rats fought in North Africa in WWII.
explanation.definitionFit: The Desert Rats were the British 7th Armoured Division, so one is a British soldier.
